ap_physics_1-f01.title: Block on a table connected to a hanging block

stimulus.description: A block of mass $m_1=3\text{ kg}$ rests on a horizontal table. A light string attached to the block passes over a light, frictionless pulley at the edge of the table and supports a hanging block of mass $m_2=2\text{ kg}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the table is $\mu=0.15$. The system is released from rest and the blocks accelerate.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: On the dot below, which represents the block of mass $m_1$, draw and label the forces (not components) that act on it while it slides. Each force must be represented by a distinct arrow starting on the dot.
parts.model_answer: Four arrows from the dot: weight down, normal up (equal length to the weight), tension toward the pulley (longer than friction), and kinetic friction opposite to the motion.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws and labels the four forces: weight, normal force, tension, and kinetic friction (no extra force such as a force of motion)
common_errors: adds a forward force of motion

rubric_rows.criterion: Arrow directions are correct: weight down, normal up, tension toward the pulley, friction opposite to the motion
common_errors: friction drawn in the direction of motion

rubric_rows.criterion: Relative lengths are consistent with the motion: the vertical arrows are equal and the tension arrow is longer than the friction arrow

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnitude of the acceleration of the blocks in terms of $m_1$, $m_2$, $\mu$, and fundamental constants.
parts.model_answer: $m_2g-T=m_2a$ and $T-\mu m_1g=m_1a$, so $a=\dfrac{(m_2-\mu m_1)g}{m_1+m_2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Applies Newton's second law to the hanging block: $m_2g-T=m_2a$
Applies Newton's second law to the table block with friction $\mu m_1 g$: $T-\mu m_1g=m_1a$
required_elements: T - mu m1 g = m1 a

rubric_rows.criterion: Combines the equations to the correct expression $a=(m_2-\mu m_1)g/(m_1+m_2)$

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the numerical value of the acceleration for $m_1=3\text{ kg}$, $m_2=2\text{ kg}$, $\mu=0.15$.
parts.model_answer: $a\approx 3.04\text{ m/s}^2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the acceleration (about 3.04)
Reports the value with correct units of meters per second squared

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The tabletop is replaced by a surface with a larger coefficient of kinetic friction. Does the tension in the string increase, decrease, or stay the same? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The tension increases. A larger friction force reduces the acceleration, so the hanging block needs a smaller net downward force and the string must support more of its weight: $T=m_2(g-a)$ with a smaller $a$.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the tension increases
common_errors: states the tension decreases because friction opposes motion

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies with Newton's second law for the hanging block: a smaller acceleration means a larger tension $T=m_2(g-a)$
common_errors: argues only that friction is larger

parts.prompt: On the dot below, which represents the block of mass $m_1$, draw and label the forces (not components) that act on it while it slides. Each force must be represented by a distinct arrow starting on the dot.
parts.model_answer: Four arrows from the dot: weight down, normal up (equal length to the weight), tension toward the pulley (longer than friction), and kinetic friction opposite to the motion.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws and labels the four forces: weight, normal force, tension, and kinetic friction (no extra force such as a force of motion)
common_errors: adds a forward force of motion

rubric_rows.criterion: Arrow directions are correct: weight down, normal up, tension toward the pulley, friction opposite to the motion
common_errors: friction drawn in the direction of motion

rubric_rows.criterion: Relative lengths are consistent with the motion: the vertical arrows are equal and the tension arrow is longer than the friction arrow

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnitude of the acceleration of the blocks in terms of $m_1$, $m_2$, $\mu$, and fundamental constants.
parts.model_answer: $m_2g-T=m_2a$ and $T-\mu m_1g=m_1a$, so $a=\dfrac{(m_2-\mu m_1)g}{m_1+m_2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Applies Newton's second law to the hanging block: $m_2g-T=m_2a$
Applies Newton's second law to the table block with friction $\mu m_1 g$: $T-\mu m_1g=m_1a$

rubric_rows.criterion: Combines the equations to the correct expression $a=(m_2-\mu m_1)g/(m_1+m_2)$

ap_physics_1-f02.title: Experiment: spring constant from the period of an oscillator

stimulus.description: A student measures the period $T$ of a block of mass $m$ hanging on a vertical spring of unknown spring constant $k$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe an experimental procedure to collect the data for the period as a function of mass. Include the equipment and the measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce the uncertainty in the measured period.
parts.model_answer: Measure each hanging mass with a balance (or use slotted masses of known mass) and use a stopwatch to time 10 oscillations for each of several hanging masses added one at a time to the same spring, starting each trial from the same small displacement, then divide by 10; repeat each timing.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the measured quantities and equipment: a balance or known masses and a timing device (both a way to know the mass and a way to time the motion are needed)
required_elements: a way to know the mass and a way to time the motion
common_errors: omits how the period is measured

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the hanging mass while keeping the spring and the starting amplitude the same (both conditions are needed)
required_elements: change only the mass and keep the same starting amplitude

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces timing uncertainty by timing many oscillations and dividing, or by repeating the trials and averaging (either earns the point)
required_elements: time many oscillations or repeat trials (either earns the point)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Using the relationship between the period of a mass on a spring, the mass and the spring constant from the reference information, identify the quantities that should be plotted on the vertical and horizontal axes so that the data produce a straight line whose slope can be used to find $k$.
parts.model_answer: Plot $T^2$ on the vertical axis against $m$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $4\pi^2/k$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $T^2$ (vertical) versus $m$ (horizontal)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On a blank grid whose scale you choose, plot the data in a form that gives a straight line, and draw a best-fit line. Label the axes with quantities and units and use a scale that fills most of the grid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Axes are labeled with quantities and units and the scale fills most of the grid
common_errors: scale uses less than half the grid

rubric_rows.criterion: Plots the five points $(m, T^2)$ accurately
Draws a straight best-fit line through the trend of the points

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Use the best-fit line to determine the spring constant $k$. Show your work.
parts.model_answer: Slope $\approx 2.00\text{ s}^2/\text{kg}$, so $k=4\pi^2/\text{slope}\approx 19.8\text{ N/m}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 2.00 s^2/kg; accept any value within 5 percent)
common_errors: uses data points rather than points on the line

rubric_rows.criterion: Relates the slope to the spring constant: slope $=4\pi^2/k$
Calculates $k$ (about 20; accept any value within 8 percent) with units of newtons per meter
alt_solutions: a value of k consistent with the student's own slope from D1, $k=4\pi^2/\text{slope}$
